You get a `collections` array back, one entry per collection, where `collection` returns a bare `tags`.

tags.description: The complete tag set, as names — REPLACES what is there. Duplicates differing only in case collapse to one. Mutually exclusive with `add_tags`/`remove_tags`.

add_tags.description: Names to add, leaving the collection's other tags alone. A tag it already carries is a no-op rather than an error.

remove_tags.description: Names to remove, leaving the collection's other tags alone. A tag it does not carry is a no-op. Removes the tag from THIS collection only — the workspace vocabulary is untouched (that is `delete_collection_tag`).

tools.name: update_collection_tag
tools.title: Rename or merge a collection tag

annotations.title: Rename or merge a collection tag

tools.description: Rename or MERGE a collection tag across the whole workspace. Merging is `merge_into`, and ONLY `merge_into`: a rename onto a name the workspace already holds is REFUSED and tells you what it clashed with, rather than quietly folding the two together. Fixing `marketing` beside `Marketing` is a merge and usually the right one, but it deletes a tag off every collection carrying it and cannot be undone, so it is worth a sentence to the user before you ask for it by name. Every change lands on every collection carrying the tag at once (`list_collection_tags` gives you the counts). Needs the workspace's tag-edit permission. Requires OAuth.

workspace.description: Workspace name, slug, or id.

merge_into.description: Name of the tag to fold this one into. This tag is then removed and every collection carrying it ends up carrying the target. The only way to merge: a `name` that collides is refused instead.

tools.name: delete_collection_tag
tools.title: Delete collection tag
tools.description: Delete a collection tag from the workspace, untagging every collection carrying it. The collections themselves are untouched — only the label goes. Irreversible, and it affects everyone in the workspace, so check the count with `list_collection_tags` and confirm with the user first. To fold a tag into another instead of losing it, use `update_collection_tag` with `merge_into`. Needs the workspace's tag-edit permission. Requires OAuth.

workspace.description: Workspace name, slug, or id.

tools.name: list_notebooks
tools.title: List notebooks
tools.description: List the notebooks inside a collection you can access — the ones you own AND ones shared to you, including view-only shares (listing is a read, so it doesn't require edit access). A notebook is a named sub-group of memos within one collection (a divider tab inside it). Every row carries `has_instructions`: true means the notebook's author wrote STANDING INSTRUCTIONS for it (how that notebook is meant to be used). Pass `include_instructions: true` to get the text itself back on each row, and follow it for work you do in that notebook. Pass `collection` as an id, slug, or name. By default archived notebooks are excluded; pass `include_archived: true` to see them too. Requires OAuth.

collection.description: The parent collection: id, slug, or name.

include_instructions.description: Return each notebook's full standing-instructions text alongside the `has_instructions` flag (default false).

tools.name: get_notebook
tools.title: Read notebook
tools.description: Read ONE notebook in full: name, description, standing `instructions` (with `instructions_updated_at` / `instructions_updated_by`), memo count, its saved `views` (the tabs scoped to this notebook), and the two layers of instructions above it: the parent collection's as `collection_instructions` and the workspace's as `workspace_instructions`, each only when written. Call this to orient yourself before working in a notebook. Memos are NOT included: list them with `list_collection_memos` or `search_memos`, passing `notebook`. Pass `include_instructions_history: true` for the last ten writes to the notebook's instructions. Pass `notebook` as a notebook id (from `list_notebooks`, `get_collection`, or `get_memo`). Requires OAuth.

include_instructions_history.description: Also return `instructions_history`: the last ten writes to this notebook's instructions. Default false.

tools.name: create_notebook
tools.title: Create notebook
tools.description: Create a notebook inside a collection you own or can edit. NOT idempotent: if an active notebook with the same (case-insensitive) name already exists in that collection, the call fails with a `conflict` so agents can't fork. Pass `collection` (id, slug, or name) plus a `name`. Pass `instructions` to give the notebook STANDING INSTRUCTIONS at creation: author-written guidance on how it is meant to be used, handed to whoever (human or agent) works in it later. Set or edit them afterwards with `update_notebook`, and read them back with `get_notebook` or `list_notebooks` (`include_instructions: true`). Lifecycle is create / archive / unarchive (no delete from MCP). Requires OAuth.

collection.description: The parent collection: id, slug, or name.

description.description: Optional longer description. Max 2000 chars.

instructions.description: Optional standing instructions for anyone working in this notebook: how it is meant to be used, what belongs in it, the conventions to follow. Prose, not a document. Max 10000 chars.

tools.name: update_notebook
tools.title: Edit notebook (name, description, instructions)
tools.description: Edit a notebook's name, description, and/or STANDING INSTRUCTIONS (the author-written brief handed to anyone working in this notebook). The memos and their memberships are untouched. Pass the notebook id (from `list_notebooks` or `get_memo`) plus a new `name`, `description`, and/or ONE instructions edit: `instructions` replaces the text wholesale (read it first with `get_notebook`; empty string clears description or instructions), `append_instructions` adds to it, or `patch_instructions` applies a unified diff. Every instructions write is recorded with its author and time. NOT idempotent against name clashes within the collection. Requires OAuth and edit access to the parent collection.

description.description: New description; empty string clears it. Max 2000 chars.

instructions.description: REPLACE the standing instructions wholesale with this text; empty string clears them. Read the current text first (get_collection / get_notebook / list_workspaces with include_instructions) so you do not drop rules you did not see. Max 10000 chars. Exclusive with `append_instructions` and `patch_instructions`.

append_instructions.description: ADD this text after the current instructions (a blank line between). The safe way to add one rule: nothing already written is touched or resent. Exclusive with `instructions` and `patch_instructions`.

patch_instructions.description: A unified diff (the same grammar `patch_memo` takes) against the current instructions text, for a one-line correction inside a long brief. Hunks are found by their lines; line numbers are optional. A hunk whose lines no longer match, or match in several places, is refused, so re-read and rebuild the diff. Exclusive with `instructions` and `append_instructions`.

tools.name: update_workspace
tools.title: Edit workspace instructions
tools.description: Write a workspace's STANDING INSTRUCTIONS: the preamble every agent working anywhere in the workspace should read first (how collections are named, what the standard notebooks mean, where to look for more, what not to restructure). This is the top of the hierarchy; `update_collection` and `update_notebook` write the two layers below it, and every collection or notebook read echoes this text as `workspace_instructions`. Three ways to edit, exactly one per call: `instructions` replaces the whole text (read it first), `append_instructions` adds a rule without resending the rest, and `patch_instructions` applies a unified diff for a one-line change. Every write is recorded with its author and time (`list_workspaces` shows `instructions_updated_by`; `include_instructions_history` returns earlier versions). Workspace owner or admin only. Pass `workspace` as a name, slug, or id from `list_workspaces`. Requires OAuth.

workspace.description: Workspace to edit (name, slug, or id).

instructions.description: REPLACE the standing instructions wholesale with this text; empty string clears them. Read the current text first (get_collection / get_notebook / list_workspaces with include_instructions) so you do not drop rules you did not see. Max 10000 chars. Exclusive with `append_instructions` and `patch_instructions`.

append_instructions.description: ADD this text after the current instructions (a blank line between). The safe way to add one rule: nothing already written is touched or resent. Exclusive with `instructions` and `patch_instructions`.

patch_instructions.description: A unified diff (the same grammar `patch_memo` takes) against the current instructions text, for a one-line correction inside a long brief. Hunks are found by their lines; line numbers are optional. A hunk whose lines no longer match, or match in several places, is refused, so re-read and rebuild the diff. Exclusive with `instructions` and `append_instructions`.

tools.name: add_memo_to_notebook
tools.title: Add memo to notebook
tools.description: Add a memo to a notebook. A notebook member must live in the notebook's parent collection, so this AUTO-ADDS the memo to that collection if it isn't already in it (the response says so). Idempotent. Pass `memo` and `notebook` ids, and optional `pinned`; pass `memos` (a list of ids) instead of `memo` to add several in one call. Requires OAuth, edit access to the memo, and edit access to the parent collection.

memos.description: Several memo ids INSTEAD of `memo`, applied in one call. Partial success: each entry reports its own `ok` or `error`, and the summary carries `applied` and `failed`, so one refusal never costs you the rest of the batch. At most 100 per call, refused rather than truncated.

pinned.description: Optional. Pin the memo to the top of the notebook.

tools.name: remove_memo_from_notebook
tools.title: Remove memo from notebook
tools.description: Remove a memo from one notebook. The memo stays in the parent collection (use `remove_memo_from_collection` to remove it from the collection, which also removes it from every notebook of that collection). Idempotent. Pass `memo` and `notebook` ids, or `memos` (a list of ids) instead of `memo` to remove several in one call. Requires OAuth, edit access to the memo, and edit access to the parent collection.

memos.description: Several memo ids INSTEAD of `memo`, applied in one call. Partial success: each entry reports its own `ok` or `error`, and the summary carries `applied` and `failed`, so one refusal never costs you the rest of the batch. At most 100 per call, refused rather than truncated.

tools.name: set_notebook_pin
tools.title: Pin memo in notebook
tools.description: Pin or unpin a memo within a notebook. Pinned members sort first in the notebook's list views. The memo must already be a member of the notebook (pinning a non-member is a no-op). Idempotent. Pass `memo` and `notebook` ids plus `pinned` (true to pin, false to unpin). Requires OAuth, edit access to the memo, and edit access to the parent collection.

pinned.description: true to pin the memo, false to unpin it.

tools.name: set_collection_pin
tools.title: Pin memo in collection
tools.description: Pin or unpin a memo within a collection. A pinned memo leads that collection's list views, ahead of whatever the view's own sort says, which is what pinning means. The collection-level twin of `set_notebook_pin`. The memo must already be filed in the collection (pinning a non-member is a no-op, reported as `changed: false`). Idempotent. Pass `memo` and `collection` (an id, slug, or name) plus `pinned` (true to pin, false to unpin), or `memos` (a list of ids) instead of `memo` to pin several in one call. Requires OAuth and edit access to the collection: a pin arranges the collection, so it is gated like filing a memo into it rather than on the memo itself.

memos.description: Several memo ids INSTEAD of `memo`, applied in one call. Partial success: each entry reports its own `ok` or `error`, and the summary carries `applied` and `failed`, so one refusal never costs you the rest of the batch. At most 100 per call, refused rather than truncated.

pinned.description: true to pin the memo, false to unpin it.

tools.name: list_views
tools.title: List collection views
tools.description: List the saved views on a collection: the shared tabs (smart lists, boards, canvases) that everyone who can see the collection also sees. Identify the collection by `collection` (an id, slug, or name). Pass `notebook` (a notebook id) to list only that notebook's tabs; otherwise you get every view on the collection, and each row names its `notebook` (null means a collection-level view spanning every memo in the collection, including memos filed in notebooks). Each view carries `display` (list, board, canvas, table, calendar, or timeline), its `where` filter in the same grammar the listing tools accept, its `sort`, a board's or a timeline's `group_by` field, its `description` (a note on what the view silently depends on, e.g. "only items with roadmap visibility = Yes appear here"; read it before building a similar view), its `group_by_scope` ("collection" reads the memo's values on ITS EDGE into this collection, "memo" reads the memo's own front matter) and `columns` layout, `card_properties`, and `protected`: `protected: true` marks a scope's own List tab (`display: "list"`), ordinary to edit (rename, filter, sort, layout, reorder). Every collection keeps exactly one, which `delete_view` refuses to delete. A notebook starts with one but may have none: its List view can be deleted while the notebook has another view, and the notebook then opens on its first remaining view. The collection, and each notebook, also has a DEFAULT view a collection manager picks: the tab a person opens it on unless they chose another tab themselves (a default that was deleted falls back to List). `save_view` with `make_default: true` sets it. Each view also carries `include_files`: true means a list, board, table, calendar or timeline view shows the collection's (or notebook's) FILES as items next to its memos, filtered and sorted by the same rules. To read a view's memos, run `list_collection_memos` with the view's `where` (for a board, group the rows by its `group_by` field yourself); for its files, run `list_assets` on the same collection or notebook with the same `where` (on a collection, add `include_notebook_files: true`). A calendar view carries `calendar`: `start` (the date or Date range property it is drawn from, `memo:<name>` for front matter, or `computed:created_at` / `computed:updated_at`), `end` (the end of a start and end pair, or null), `color_by` (a select whose option colours tint its bars, or null), `week_start`, `show_weekends`, `default_layout` (month or week) and, when set, `density` (expanded: week view's cards in month view; stacked: one continuous timeline with the days down the side, each memo a card spanning its days). To read what a calendar shows for a month, run `list_collection_memos` with the view's `where` plus an `overlaps` clause on `start` (for a pair, `{"field": <start>, "lte": <last day>}` and `{"field": <end>, "gte": <first day>}`, or the start alone in the month when the end is empty). A timeline view carries `timeline`: `start`, `end` and `color_by` as a calendar's, `week_start`, and `default_zoom` (week, month, quarter or year: how far it opens zoomed). Its rows are grouped into swimlanes by `group_by` (null: one list), ordered within each group by `sort` (none: start date, then end date, then title); `columns` holds the group `order`, `hidden` groups and `collapsed` groups. Read a timeline's period the same way as a calendar's month. Every row also carries `url`, the link that OPENS that tab, and the response carries `collection_url` for the collection itself. A view is addressed as `?view=<view id>` on its collection's page (a notebook view on the notebook's page), so you can hand a person a link straight to the board you built. The two reserved values `list` and `canvas` also work in that parameter and name the built-in tabs (on a notebook with no List or Canvas view they open its first view). Requires OAuth.

notebook.description: Optional notebook id: list only that notebook's views.

tools.name: save_view
tools.title: Save collection view
tools.description: Create or update a saved view on a collection. A view is a shared tab that everyone who can see the collection also sees (a smart list, a board, or a canvas), so save one when the team should keep it; for a one-off query use `list_collection_memos` with `where` instead. Omit `view_id` to create; pass it to update, which replaces the whole stored definition (omitted optional parts are cleared, so send the full view each time). `display` is "list", "board", "canvas", "table", "calendar" or "timeline". `where` stores a filter in the shared grammar the listing tools accept (each clause reads front matter, or the collection's own value with `scope: "collection"`); the view's membership is live, and a malformed filter is rejected with the same instructive error the listing tools give rather than saved broken. `sort` ({field, direction: "asc" | "desc"}) orders the view. A board additionally requires `group_by` (the field whose values become its columns), may carry `group_by_scope` to say which layer that field reads (see its own description), and may carry `columns` (the column `order` array plus a `hidden` array); all three are board-only. A calendar requires `calendar_start` (the date or Date range property it is drawn from) and takes the other flat `calendar_*` parameters (each described on its own); they are calendar-only and refused on any other display. A calendar can't be drawn from a property that isn't a date or a Date range; `calendar_end` pairs only with a plain date start; `calendar_color_by` must be a select. A timeline requires `timeline_start` and takes the other flat `timeline_*` parameters by the same rules; it may also carry `group_by` and `group_by_scope` (its swimlanes, optional: omit for one list) and `columns` (the group `order`, `hidden` groups and `collapsed` groups). `card_properties` (and `sort.field`) name properties by SOURCE: a collection property by its name (`status`), the memo's own front matter with a `memo:` prefix (`memo:status`), and a computed property with a `computed:` prefix: `computed:notebook` (the memo's notebook name in this collection), `computed:created_at` / `computed:updated_at` (the memo's Created at / Updated at timestamps), and `computed:created_by` / `computed:updated_by` (the memo's Created by / Last updated by people). A collection property and a front-matter property of the same name are two properties; nothing falls back from one to the other. A plain name the collection doesn't define is saved as front matter. Pass `notebook` (a notebook id in the collection) to put the tab on that notebook; otherwise the view is collection-level and spans every memo in the collection, including memos filed in notebooks. `description` is an optional note on the view (what it depends on, why a card might be missing), shown to people on the tab and to agents in `list_views`; it filters nothing. Any editor of the collection can save views. Updating the `protected` List view (see `list_views`) is ordinary EXCEPT `display` must stay "list" and `notebook` must stay whatever it already is, since it is that collection's or notebook's own List view, so both are refused. The response carries `url`, the link that opens the saved view, so you can tell the person where it is. `make_default: true` also makes the saved view the default tab of its scope (the collection, or its notebook): where a person lands unless they picked another tab themselves. It needs a collection manager and never changes the tab order. Requires OAuth.

notebook.description: Optional notebook id: the view becomes a tab on that notebook instead of the whole collection.

view_id.description: Update this existing view instead of creating one.

description.description: Optional note on the view: what it silently depends on, or why an item might be missing from it. Shown on the tab's tooltip and returned by `list_views`. Empty string clears. Max 500 chars.

display.description: How the view renders: list, board, canvas, table, calendar, or timeline. A table's columns come from card_properties. A calendar draws memos from `calendar_start` on a month or week grid (or a stacked timeline, see `calendar_density`), with undated memos in a No date tray. A timeline draws one row per memo on one boundless horizontal time axis from `timeline_start`, its bars spanning their dates, rows grouped by `group_by` and sorted within each group. A timeline has no No date tray: a memo with no readable date is a row with an empty track, last in its group.

timeline_start.description: Timeline views only (and required for them): the property that places each memo on the timeline, by the same rules as `calendar_start`: a collection Date range or date by name, `memo:<name>` for front matter, or `computed:created_at` / `computed:updated_at` (read only).

timeline_end.description: Timeline views only: a second DATE property that ends each item, pairing with a plain date `timeline_start`.

timeline_color_by.description: Timeline views only: a SELECT property whose option colours tint the bars. Omit for neutral bars.

timeline_week_start.description: Timeline views only: where week ticks fall at Week and Month zoom. Default monday.

timeline_default_zoom.description: Timeline views only: how far the timeline is zoomed when someone opens it (each person's own zoom wins after that). Default month.

calendar_start.description: Calendar views only (and required for them): the property the calendar is drawn from. A collection property by name (a Date range, or a date), the memo's own front matter as `memo:<name>`, or `computed:created_at` / `computed:updated_at` (read only).

calendar_end.description: Calendar views only: a second DATE property that ends each item, making a start and end pair with `calendar_start` (which must then be a plain date, not a Date range). Omit for a range or a single date.

calendar_color_by.description: Calendar views only: a SELECT property whose option colours tint the bars. Omit for neutral bars.

calendar_week_start.description: Calendar views only: the first day of each week row. Default monday.

calendar_show_weekends.description: Calendar views only: false hides Saturday and Sunday. Default true.

calendar_default_layout.description: Calendar views only: the layout the calendar opens in for someone who hasn't picked one. Default month.

calendar_density.description: Calendar views only: the calendar's layout. compact (default) fits three one-line bars a day in month view before "N more"; expanded draws week view's two-line cards (time, card properties) in month view, each week row growing to fit them, with no "N more"; stacked shows one continuous timeline of months with the days down the side, each memo a card spanning its days, overlaps cascading, instead of a grid, at any width.

where.description: Optional field filter: an array of clauses that must ALL match, applied in the database so `limit`/`offset` page over the matches. A clause reads the memo's own front matter unless it says `scope: "collection"`, which reads that collection's OWN value instead (only in a call scoped to one collection: `list_collection_memos`, or `search_memos`/`list_my_memos` with `collection` or `notebook`). A collection property and a front-matter property of the same name are two properties: nothing falls back from one to the other. Each clause names a `field` plus ZERO or more operators: `equals` (deep equality: strings, numbers, booleans, null, arrays, objects), `not_equals` (value differs, and a memo WITHOUT the field also matches: "status is not Done" keeps unset ones; add `exists: true` for "has a value and it isn't"), `in` (present and equal to any listed value), `not_in` (equal to none, absent included), `exists` (true = field present, false = field absent), `contains` (array field: has an element equal to the value; string field: substring), `contains_any` / `contains_all` / `contains_none` (each an array of values, for a multi-select or list: holds at least one, every one, or none of them; a single stored value counts as a one-item set, and `contains_none` also matches a memo WITHOUT the field), `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte` (ordered comparison, strictly same-type: a stored NUMBER against a number operand compares numerically, a stored STRING against a string operand compares lexicographically, which orders ISO-8601 date strings correctly; any other pairing, including booleans, null, arrays, objects, absent fields, or a number-vs-string mix, never matches; note that values written before typed ingest may be stored as strings, e.g. "726", which will not match numeric comparisons until migrated). Against a plain date operand (`2026-09-30`), a stored date, timed date or Date range compares by the calendar day it STARTS on, so `lte: "2026-09-30"` keeps `2026-09-30T10:00` and `gt`/`lt` read as "starts after"/"starts before". `overlaps` (an object with optional `from` and `to` days) matches a date or Date range that touches that window, e.g. `{"overlaps": {"from": "2026-10-01", "to": "2026-10-31"}}`. A clause with only `field` is a presence check. Several operators on ONE clause all apply, ANDed together, so a range is a single clause: `where: [{"field": "active_clients", "gte": 400, "lte": 420}]` matches memos whose `active_clients` is a number from 400 to 420 inclusive. A malformed clause is NOT ignored: any key that is not `field` or an operator (e.g. a misspelled operator name), a non-array `in`/`not_in`, a non-boolean `exists`, or a missing `field` rejects the whole call with an error naming the bad clause, rather than silently returning unfiltered results. Example: memos not rated green, unrated ones included: `where: [{"field": "overall", "not_equals": "green"}]` (add `include_fields: true` to see each match's rating); only the rated ones: `{"field": "overall", "exists": true, "not_equals": "green"}`.

scope.description: Optional. Which property the clause reads: "collection" for the collection's own value, "memo" for the memo's own front matter. Omitted, the clause reads front matter.

overlaps.description: For a date or Date range property: the value touches the window of days from `from` to `to` (YYYY-MM-DD, both inclusive, either left out for an open side). A single date counts as a one-day range. Example: everything in October 2026: `{"field": "dates", "overlaps": {"from": "2026-10-01", "to": "2026-10-31"}}`.

group_by.description: Board views (required) and timeline views (optional): the field whose values become the board's columns, or the timeline's groups of rows. `notebook` groups by notebook. A multi-select or a Date range can't group either.

group_by_scope.description: Board and timeline views, and only alongside group_by. Whether the columns come from this collection's own value for the field ("collection": what this memo's status is JUST IN THIS collection) or from the memo's own front matter ("memo": the same value that field holds everywhere the memo appears). A field can hold both, and they are separate properties, so pick the one you mean. Omitted, it is "collection" when the collection defines the field, else "memo". A front-matter board's columns are the values in use, in a neutral tone, in the view's saved column order.

columns.description: Board and timeline views. Column (or group) layout: `order` lists column values in display order, `hidden` lists column values to hide. A timeline may also list `collapsed` groups, shown collapsed for everyone.

card_properties.description: Properties shown on each card or row, by source: a collection property by name, the memo's own front matter as `memo:<name>`, or a computed property with a `computed:` prefix (for example `computed:notebook`, the memo's notebook name in this collection; `computed:created_at` and `computed:updated_at`, the memo's Created at and Updated at timestamps; `computed:created_by` and `computed:updated_by`, the memo's Created by and Last updated by people). A plain name the collection doesn't define is saved as front matter, except a bare `notebook`, which an older view stored for the computed property and still reads that way. On a view that shows files, `computed:item_kind` (Memo or File) and `computed:file_type` (PDF, CSV, Link and so on) are available too. A list view shows each memo's notebook beside its title unless this list holds `computed:notebook:hidden`. A table view shows the memo title as a column of its own, first unless this list holds `computed:title`, which puts it at that place instead, and hidden when the list holds `computed:title:hidden` (rows still open on click).

include_files.description: List, board, table, calendar and timeline views: whether the view shows the collection's files (files and links added to the collection or its notebooks) as items next to its memos. Files carry the collection's properties, so they group, filter and sort like memos; filter them with `computed:item_kind` (Memo or File) or `computed:file_type` (for example PDF). Defaults to true for a new view; omit it on an update to keep the view's current setting. Views saved before files could be items have it off. Has no effect on a canvas (which already shows files) or on the protected List view (which lists files in its own section).

make_default.description: Make this view the default tab of its scope (the collection, or the notebook it is on) after saving it. Collection managers only.

tools.name: delete_view
tools.title: Delete collection view
tools.description: Delete a saved view by `view_id` (get ids from `list_views`). The shared tab disappears for everyone who sees the collection; the memos in the view are not touched (a view is a saved way of looking, not a container). Any editor of the collection can delete its views, with two refusals: a collection-level `protected` List view (every collection keeps one), and a notebook's last remaining view (a notebook always keeps at least one tab). A notebook's own `protected` List view can be deleted while the notebook has another view; the notebook then opens on its first remaining view. Requires OAuth.

tools.name: list_field_definitions
tools.title: List collection properties
tools.description: List a collection's PROPERTIES and, for each, the option set a board groups by. This is the schema, not values: `list_fields` tells you what one memo holds, this tells you what the collection has DEFINED. Each row carries `field_name`, `field_type` (select, multi_select, person, date, date_range, number, text...; a collection property is never `list`, several values are a `multi_select`; a `date_range` value is one ISO 8601 interval string, `2026-10-12/2026-10-23`, or a single date), `options` (label + colour, for a select or multi_select, each optionally with its own `description`), `hidden`, and `description`: what the property MEANS and when to set it, written by whoever defined it (e.g. "roadmap visibility = Yes is what puts an item on the roadmap board"). Read descriptions before setting values; write them with `set_field_definition`. `options: null` means the property exists but no option set was ever registered; `[]` means one was registered and is deliberately empty. A `person` property has NO options — its vocabulary is the workspace roster, returned on that row as `people` (`{display, email, role}`). Write the `display` string EXACTLY as listed (an email for the same person is accepted and stored as the display name); `set_field` refuses a person value that names nobody, because a name the app cannot resolve assigns work to no one while still looking assigned. Guests invited to a specific memo are accepted there too, though only members are listed here. Read this BEFORE building a board: a board's columns come from the registered options plus whatever values the loaded rows actually carry, so a value you set that is not a registered option only becomes a column while a card carries it. A column you name in a view's `columns.order` that is neither is dropped without warning. Identify the collection by `collection` (an id, slug, or name). Requires OAuth.

tools.name: set_field_definition
tools.title: Set collection property options
tools.description: Define, describe, rename, or delete a collection PROPERTY — mutually exclusive modes on one tool, picked by which of `options`, `rename_to`, or `delete` you pass (at most one), plus `description`, which rides alongside `options` or stands alone. DESCRIBE (pass `description`, alone or with `options`): records what the property MEANS and when to set it, shown to people as a tooltip on the property and returned to agents by `list_field_definitions`. Alone, it changes nothing else (type and options stay as stored). Each option may carry its own `description` too. Empty string clears. Max 500 chars. DEFINE (pass `options`): sets the property's option set and type. This is how a board gets columns. Setting a value with `set_field` records the value and does NOT register it as an option, so a board grouped by that property shows a column only while some card carries the value. register the options here and the columns exist whether or not anything is in them yet. `options` REPLACES the whole set (send every option you want to keep, in the order you want them); an empty list clears them deliberately, which is different from never having set any. Each option is `{label, color}`, and `color` is genuinely optional: omit it and the option takes a stable colour derived from its label, so you only name one when you actually care. When you do name one it must be a palette token, and the schema's `enum` lists them all. REMOVING an option (leaving it out of the set) CLEARS that value from every card holding it, memo or file, and the response reports how many in `values_cleared`. Read the current options with `list_field_definitions` first so you don't drop one by accident. Renaming an OPTION LABEL here does NOT move memos already on the old label; use `rename_field_option` for that. RENAME (pass `rename_to`): renames the PROPERTY itself from `field` to `rename_to`, carrying its type, its options, and every memo's stored value across to the new name — a board keeps its columns and its cards. Refused with `invalid_input` if `rename_to` is already another property on this collection (rename or delete that one first), or if `rename_to` is a SYSTEM name (owner, assignee, reviewer, approver, due, due_date, deadline, start_date, end_date, status, done) and the property isn't already that name's type. DELETE (pass `delete: true`): removes the property outright. Its definition AND every memo's and file's stored value under it in this collection are gone, reported as `memos_cleared` and `files_cleared`. NOT reversible; a memo's own front matter under the same name (if it happens to share it) is untouched. CLEAR VALUES (pass `clear_values: true`): removes every memo's and file's value for this property in this collection in ONE call, and KEEPS the property: its type, options, colours and every view built on it stay as they are. Reported as `memos_cleared` and `files_cleared`. Use it when moving values off the collection (e.g. onto each memo's own front matter) instead of one `delete_field` per card; writing `null` per card does not clear, it stores an explicit null. NOT reversible. Organising, so it never counts against the automated-write allowance. Requires edit access to the collection, and OAuth.

field.description: Property name, e.g. "stage". In rename mode, this is the CURRENT name.

description.description: DESCRIBE mode, alone or with `options`: what this property means and when to set it, for people (a tooltip) and agents (`list_field_definitions`). Empty string clears. Max 500 chars.

options.description: DEFINE mode. The complete option set, in order. Replaces what is stored. Omit when passing `rename_to` or `delete`.

description.description: Optional. What picking this option means (e.g. "XL: more than a sprint"). Max 500 chars.

color.description: Optional. One of the palette tokens listed in `enum`. Omitted, the option gets a stable colour derived from its own label, so registering a vocabulary never fails on a colour you had no opinion about.

field_type.description: DEFINE mode only. Property type. `select` (one value) and `multi_select` (several values) carry options, a managed set with colours. A collection property has no `list` type: `list` is accepted and stored as `multi_select`, and the response says so. Sent without `options`, a select or multi-select keeps its current ones and any other type carries none. Converting a select to multi_select registers every value in use as an option (refused over 100). `date_range` holds a date or a span as one ISO 8601 interval string (`2026-10-12/2026-10-23`), and can't group a board. Omitted, it keeps the stored type, else defaults to the reserved type for the NAME (`owner` and `assignee` are person, `due` is date, `budget` is number...) and only then to select, so registering options never retypes a property. SYSTEM names (owner, assignee, reviewer, approver, due, due_date, deadline, start_date, end_date, status, done) keep their type: another type is refused with `invalid_input`. Every other well-known name only suggests a default and can be given any type.

rename_to.description: RENAME mode. The new property name. `field` is read as the current name. Cannot be combined with `options`, `field_type`, or `delete`.

delete.description: DELETE mode. Remove this property definition and every memo's stored value under it in this collection. Not reversible. Cannot be combined with `options`, `field_type`, or `rename_to`.

clear_values.description: CLEAR VALUES mode. Remove every memo's and file's value for this property in this collection, keeping the property and its options. Not reversible. Cannot be combined with any other mode.

drop_range_ends.description: DEFINE mode, changing a `date_range` property to `date` only. That change keeps each value's start and drops its end, so it is refused with the number of ranges that would lose an end until you send `drop_range_ends: true` with the same call.

tools.name: rename_field_option
tools.title: Rename a property option
tools.description: Rename ONE option on a collection property, carrying every memo and file already on the old label across to the new one. This is the difference between this tool and `set_field_definition`: renaming a label there edits the vocabulary only and leaves the cards behind on a value that is no longer an option, while renaming here moves the vocabulary and the values together, so a board's column keeps its cards. Identify the option by its exact current `label` (`list_field_definitions` shows them); `not_found` means no option on that property spells it that way. `new_label` is validated exactly as a saved option set is, so renaming onto a label another option on the SAME property already uses is refused rather than silently merging the two. Answers with the property's full option list plus `memos_renamed` and `files_renamed`, the number of memos and files whose value actually moved (0 is a perfectly good success: the label existed but nothing was on it). A renamed option carries its colour over untouched. Renaming reaches memos that are LOCKED or ARCHIVED, deliberately: this is the collection's own vocabulary staying consistent with the collection's own values, not an editorial change to anybody's memo, and skipping the frozen ones would leave them quietly disagreeing with everything else. Requires edit access to the collection, and OAuth.

tools.name: duplicate_memo
tools.title: Duplicate memo
tools.description: COPY a memo into a brand new memo (new id, new URLs); the original is left in place. To RELOCATE an existing memo to another workspace without copying it (keeping the same id, history, and comments), use `move_memo` instead. The copy includes content, fields, images, embedded artifacts, and optionally comments. Any role (viewer, commenter, editor) can duplicate. Returns the new memo's role URLs. The copy lands in a workspace: pass `workspace` (name, slug, or id from `list_workspaces`) to choose; with `keep_collections` it adopts the source collections' workspace instead. If you belong to multiple workspaces and pass neither, the call returns a `workspace_required` disambiguation that lists them (it will NOT silently use whatever workspace you last opened in the web app). Ask the user which one, then retry with an explicit `workspace`, and remember their choice for the rest of this session so later writes pass it without asking again.

url.description: Full memo URL (edit, comment, or read). Preferred over id.

include_comments.description: When true, all comment threads are cloned into the copy with their anchors re-attached. Defaults to false.

keep_collections.description: When true, the copy is filed into every collection you own that the source memo is in, and adopts the first such collection's workspace (so `workspace` is ignored). Requires OAuth (only your own collections are considered); a no-op in anonymous sessions. Use `add_memo_to_collection` for finer control. Defaults to false.

workspace.description: Optional workspace for the copy (name, slug, or id from `list_workspaces`). Only needed when you belong to several workspaces and want a specific one; ignored when `keep_collections` is set (the copy adopts the source collections' workspace). When you belong to multiple workspaces and pass neither, the call returns a `workspace_required` error listing them rather than guessing.

tools.name: get_memo_image_upload_url
tools.title: Get image upload link
tools.description:
Mint a one-shot signed URL the agent can PUT a RASTER image to (PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF). Returns `{ upload_url, image_url, markdown, expires_at }`. 

NETWORK REQUIREMENT — READ BEFORE INVOKING: The PUT in step 2 below requires outbound HTTPS from your sandbox/runtime to `*.fieldwerk.ai`. Many MCP clients (notably Claude.ai web) sandbox the agent behind an egress proxy with an allowlist that does NOT include `*.fieldwerk.ai` by default. If your PUT returns HTTP 403 with a response header like `x-deny-reason: host_not_allowed`, the block is in your runtime's egress proxy — NOT in Fieldwerk — and retrying will fail the same way. When that happens: DO NOT retry. If your runtime can place the image's bytes into a tool call itself (a user attachment it already holds), use `upload_memo_image_inline` instead: the bytes travel inside the MCP call, so no outbound request is needed (images up to 1 MB). Otherwise tell the user verbatim: "Image upload requires outbound network access to *.fieldwerk.ai. On Claude.ai, this is in Settings → Privacy → Network (or similar in other MCP clients). Please enable egress to *.fieldwerk.ai, then ask me to retry." Wait for the user to confirm before retrying.

HOW TO USE THIS TOOL:
  1. Call this tool with `mime_type` matching the image you'll upload. If the image is generated at higher resolution than its intended display size (e.g. an AI-generated 1024×1024 image meant to display at ~512px, or a screenshot from a retina display), pass `pixel_density: 2` (or 3). Fieldwerk will render it at half (or third) its natural width so it stays sharp without overflowing the column.
  2. From your sandbox / Bash, PUT the image bytes to `upload_url` with `Content-Type: <mime_type>`. Example: `curl -X PUT --data-binary @file.png -H 'Content-Type: image/png' '<upload_url>'`. The bytes go directly to our worker — they never traverse this MCP channel, never go through your output tokens, never get truncated by tool-call size caps. This is the preferred way to upload an image from an agent context; `upload_memo_image_inline` is the fallback for runtimes that cannot make the PUT.
  3. On success the worker returns 200. The image is then live at `image_url`. Splice the returned `markdown` into the memo via `append_to_memo`, `replace_section`, etc.

IMPORTANT — SVG is NOT supported (security policy: SVG can carry executable script). The URL is signed to the specific `mime_type` you request; PUTting bytes of a different format will be rejected. If you do not already have a raster image to upload, DO NOT try to fabricate one by generating SVG/XML markup — the PUT will be rejected. Instead, ask the user to upload the image themselves (drag-and-drop in the memo editor) or to give you a URL to an existing raster image (use `upload_memo_image_from_url` for that case). Diagrams or other visuals the user wants are usually better expressed as text/markdown content (lists, headings, tables) than as constructed images.

The URL expires in 10 minutes and is single-use in spirit (re-PUT overwrites the same R2 object). Max body size 5 MB. Requires Clerk OAuth and edit role on the memo.

IMAGE LAYOUT: an image's size and placement live in its URL's query string, so `![alt](url)` stays plain markdown. `?size=N` (integer 10 to 100) makes the image N% of the width it has available (the column, or the wider breakout when also `?wide=1`), stretching a small image if asked. `?align=left|center|right` places it (absent: fit images sit left, wide images centred). `?wide=1` lets a big image break out of the column. Absent flags mean natural size. You can set these at upload with the `size`, `align` and `wide` inputs (the returned `markdown` carries them), or change them on an existing image by rewriting its URL in the memo body with any write tool. `?px=N` is the display width a retina upload was made for and is stamped for you from `pixel_density`; leave it alone.

size.description: Optional. Show the image at this percentage of the available width (10 to 100).

align.description: Optional. Horizontal placement. Absent: fit images sit left, wide images centred.

wide.description: Optional. Let the image break out of the prose column into the wider room the page has.

tools.name: upload_memo_image_from_url
tools.title: Upload image from URL
tools.description:
Upload a RASTER image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF) to a memo by giving the server a URL to fetch from. Use this when an image source URL is available (e.g. an image-generation tool returned a hosted URL) — it sidesteps the MCP message-size cap on the inline-base64 path. The server fetches the URL with strict guardrails (https only, our own zones / private IPs denied, manual redirects with per-hop revalidation, 5 MB cap, 10-second timeout) and stores the bytes as a memo image. Returns the hosted image URL plus pre-built markdown ready to splice into a follow-up write tool. 

IMPORTANT — `source_url` must point to a RASTER image. SVG is NOT supported (security policy) and will be rejected by the post-fetch MIME check. If the user is asking for a diagram or visual and you don't have a raster image URL, DO NOT try to fabricate one by generating SVG/XML — instead, ask the user to upload an image themselves or provide a URL to an existing raster image. Diagrams the user wants in their memo are usually better expressed as text/markdown content (lists, headings, tables) than as constructed images. 

Requires Clerk OAuth and edit role on the memo. Rate-limited to 60 fetches per hour per user.

IMAGE LAYOUT: an image's size and placement live in its URL's query string, so `![alt](url)` stays plain markdown. `?size=N` (integer 10 to 100) makes the image N% of the width it has available (the column, or the wider breakout when also `?wide=1`), stretching a small image if asked. `?align=left|center|right` places it (absent: fit images sit left, wide images centred). `?wide=1` lets a big image break out of the column. Absent flags mean natural size. You can set these at upload with the `size`, `align` and `wide` inputs (the returned `markdown` carries them), or change them on an existing image by rewriting its URL in the memo body with any write tool. `?px=N` is the display width a retina upload was made for and is stamped for you from `pixel_density`; leave it alone.

size.description: Optional. Show the image at this percentage of the available width (10 to 100).

align.description: Optional. Horizontal placement. Absent: fit images sit left, wide images centred.

wide.description: Optional. Let the image break out of the prose column into the wider room the page has.

tools.name: upload_memo_image_inline
tools.title: Upload image inline
tools.description:
Upload a RASTER image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF) to a memo by sending its bytes as base64 INSIDE this tool call. The server decodes, checks and stores them; the client makes no network request other than the MCP call itself. Returns `{ image_url, markdown, bytes, mime_type }`; splice `markdown` into the memo with `append_to_memo`, `replace_section`, etc.

WHEN TO USE IT, in order of preference:
  1. The image is already hosted somewhere: `upload_memo_image_from_url`.
  2. Your sandbox can make an outbound PUT to *.fieldwerk.ai: `get_memo_image_upload_url`. Preferred for anything large; the bytes never enter the MCP channel.
  3. Your runtime holds the image (a user attachment, say) but its egress rules block that PUT: THIS tool. Pass the attachment's bytes as base64 in `data` (a `data:image/png;base64,` prefix is fine). Only do this when the runtime supplies the base64; never type an image out token by token.

LIMITS: at most 1000000 decoded bytes (about 1 MB; base64 adds a third on top, and MCP clients cap tool-call arguments). Over that the call fails with `inline_image_too_large` and you should use path 1 or 2. `mime_type` must match the bytes: they are sniffed, and SVG or any other non-raster format is refused. If the image was made at higher resolution than its display size (a retina screenshot, a 1024px generated image meant for ~512px), pass `pixel_density: 2` (or 3). Requires Clerk OAuth and edit role on the memo. Rate-limited to 60 uploads per hour per user.

IMAGE LAYOUT: an image's size and placement live in its URL's query string, so `![alt](url)` stays plain markdown. `?size=N` (integer 10 to 100) makes the image N% of the width it has available (the column, or the wider breakout when also `?wide=1`), stretching a small image if asked. `?align=left|center|right` places it (absent: fit images sit left, wide images centred). `?wide=1` lets a big image break out of the column. Absent flags mean natural size. You can set these at upload with the `size`, `align` and `wide` inputs (the returned `markdown` carries them), or change them on an existing image by rewriting its URL in the memo body with any write tool. `?px=N` is the display width a retina upload was made for and is stamped for you from `pixel_density`; leave it alone.

data.description: The image bytes as base64 (standard or URL-safe alphabet; an optional `data:<mime>;base64,` prefix is stripped).

size.description: Optional. Show the image at this percentage of the available width (10 to 100).

align.description: Optional. Horizontal placement. Absent: fit images sit left, wide images centred.

wide.description: Optional. Let the image break out of the prose column into the wider room the page has.

tools.name: get_memo_image_url
tools.title: Get image download link
tools.description:
Get a short-lived (5-minute) signed URL that lets you DOWNLOAD a raster image embedded in a memo, for handing the file to something else. To LOOK at an image yourself, call `read_memo_image` instead: it returns the pixels inline, which works in every client, whereas this URL is only useful if your runtime can fetch URLs.

The memo's images are visible in its markdown as `![alt](https://img.fieldwerk.ai/...)`, but those public URLs are behind hotlink protection and cannot be fetched from non-browser contexts. This tool mints a time-limited URL that bypasses that restriction.

Pass the `image_url` exactly as it appears in the memo's markdown, layout flags and all (`?size=`, `?align=`, `?wide=`, `?px=` are ignored when locating the object). The URL must be on `img.fieldwerk.ai` and must belong to the memo you're reading. The returned `read_url` can be fetched with a plain GET (no auth headers needed).

Requires any access role (read, comment, or edit) on the memo.

IMAGE LAYOUT: an image's size and placement live in its URL's query string, so `![alt](url)` stays plain markdown. `?size=N` (integer 10 to 100) makes the image N% of the width it has available (the column, or the wider breakout when also `?wide=1`), stretching a small image if asked. `?align=left|center|right` places it (absent: fit images sit left, wide images centred). `?wide=1` lets a big image break out of the column. Absent flags mean natural size. You can set these at upload with the `size`, `align` and `wide` inputs (the returned `markdown` carries them), or change them on an existing image by rewriting its URL in the memo body with any write tool. `?px=N` is the display width a retina upload was made for and is stamped for you from `pixel_density`; leave it alone.

image_url.description: The full image URL from the memo's markdown, e.g. https://img.fieldwerk.ai/memos/<slug>/<id>.png

tools.name: read_memo_image
tools.title: Read image inline
tools.description:
Read a raster image embedded in a memo and return it INLINE as MCP image content, so you can look at it directly: screenshots, diagrams, photos. This is the tool to use when you need to see what an image shows; it works in every client because nothing has to fetch a URL. (`get_memo_image_url` is for downloading the file instead.)

The result has two blocks: a text block with metadata (`mime`, `width`, `height`, the stored `source_width`/`source_height`, and `resized`), then the image itself. Large images are downscaled to at most 1568px on the long edge before being returned, which keeps text in screenshots readable while bounding the payload. PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF are supported (a GIF is returned as stored; only its first frame is meaningful to a vision model).

Only call this for an image you actually need to inspect: each call costs vision tokens and up to 1.5MB of transfer. `get_memo` never inlines images itself.

Pass the `image_url` exactly as it appears in the memo's markdown, layout flags and all (`?size=`, `?align=`, `?wide=`, `?px=` are ignored when locating the object). The URL must be on `img.fieldwerk.ai` and must belong to the memo you're reading.

Requires any access role (read, comment, or edit) on the memo.

image_url.description: The full image URL from the memo's markdown, e.g. https://img.fieldwerk.ai/memos/<slug>/<id>.png

tools.name: get_memo_artifact_upload_url
tools.title: Get artifact upload link
tools.description:
Mint a one-shot signed URL the agent can PUT an HTML artifact to (self-contained HTML+CSS+JS, ≤1 MB). Returns `{ upload_url, artifact_url, markdown, expires_at }`. 

WHAT IS AN ARTIFACT — interactive content the user wants to embed in their memo: a chart, a mini-app, a calculator, a visualisation, a tic-tac-toe board. The HTML you provide will render in a sandboxed iframe on a separate origin (`fieldwerkartifacts.com`) so it can run scripts safely without touching the user's Fieldwerk session. Same shape as Claude.ai's chat-side Artifacts.

NETWORK REQUIREMENT — READ BEFORE INVOKING: the PUT requires outbound HTTPS from your sandbox to `*.fieldwerk.ai`. If the PUT returns HTTP 403 with `x-deny-reason: host_not_allowed`, your runtime is blocking it. Don't retry the PUT: send the same HTML with `upload_memo_artifact_inline` instead, which carries it inside the tool call and needs no outbound request. If your runtime can't put the HTML in a tool call either, tell the user to enable outbound to `*.fieldwerk.ai` in their MCP client's network settings.

HOW TO USE THIS TOOL:
  1. Call this tool. Returns `upload_url` (signed, 10-min TTL) and `artifact_url` (the eventual https URL the iframe will load from).
  2. From your sandbox / Bash, PUT the HTML bytes to `upload_url` with `Content-Type: text/html`. Example: `curl -X PUT --data-binary @artifact.html -H 'Content-Type: text/html' '<upload_url>'`. Bytes go directly to our worker — never through your output tokens, never truncated by tool-call size caps.
  3. Splice the returned `markdown` (a fenced ```artifact block) into the memo via `append_to_memo` / `replace_section` / etc.

CONTENT REQUIREMENTS:
  • A self-contained HTML document. Inline `<script>` and `<style>` are fine. NO external scripts, stylesheets, or fonts — the artifact origin's CSP blocks them (`script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`, no CDNs).
  • NO network calls — `connect-src 'none'`. The artifact cannot `fetch()`, XHR, WebSocket, or WebRTC anywhere.
  • NO forms, popups, top-navigation, microphone, camera, geolocation, payment. Sandbox + Permissions-Policy lock these off.
  • Images must be inline (`data:` / `blob:` URIs) or omitted.
  • Size cap: 1 MB. Keep artifacts focused — they're not full apps.

If the user asks for something the artifact CSP can't allow (loading external data, making API calls), tell them so explicitly and suggest an alternative — don't silently strip the offending bits from the HTML and upload anyway.

REVISING AN ARTIFACT THAT'S ALREADY IN THE MEMO? Don't upload a new one: use `replace_artifact` (same link, same block, old versions kept).

Requires Clerk OAuth and edit role on the memo.

tools.name: upload_memo_artifact_inline
tools.title: Upload artifact inline
tools.description:
Upload an HTML artifact to a memo by sending the HTML as text INSIDE this tool call. The server checks and stores it; the client makes no network request other than the MCP call itself. Returns `{ artifact_url, markdown, bytes }`; splice `markdown` (a fenced ```artifact block) into the memo with `append_to_memo`, `replace_section`, etc. To revise an artifact already in the memo, use `replace_artifact` instead.

WHEN TO USE IT: your runtime can't PUT to *.fieldwerk.ai (a sandbox egress proxy refused the `get_memo_artifact_upload_url` PUT, or you have no shell at all). Where the PUT works, prefer it: the HTML then never passes through your output tokens.

CONTENT REQUIREMENTS are the same as `get_memo_artifact_upload_url`'s: a self-contained HTML document (it must start with <!DOCTYPE html>, <html>, <head> or <body>), inline <script> and <style> only, no external scripts, stylesheets, fonts or network calls, images as `data:` URIs. It renders in a sandboxed iframe on `fieldwerkartifacts.com`.

LIMITS: at most 1048576 bytes of UTF-8 (1 MB, the same cap as the PUT path); over that the call fails with `inline_artifact_too_large`. Send the file's exact contents; don't retype or summarise a large file. Requires Clerk OAuth and edit role on the memo. Shares the inline upload limit of 60 per hour per user with `upload_memo_image_inline`.

html.description: The complete HTML document, as text.

tools.name: get_asset_upload_url
tools.title: Get asset upload link
tools.description:
Mint a one-shot signed URL to upload a FILE and add it to a memo (an attachment), or to a collection or notebook (a file in its Files list). Provide exactly one target. Returns `{ asset_id, upload_url, expires_at }`. 

HOW TO USE: 1) call this with the file's `content_type` (and ideally `filename`); 2) from your sandbox/Bash, PUT the bytes to `upload_url` with a matching `Content-Type` header, e.g. `curl -X PUT --data-binary @file.pdf -H 'Content-Type: application/pdf' '<upload_url>'`. Bytes go straight to our worker; they never traverse this MCP channel. On success (HTTP 200) the asset is live and listed by `list_assets` / `get_memo`. The PUT needs outbound HTTPS to `*.fieldwerk.ai`. To update an HTML file that's already there, use `replace_artifact` (same link, old versions kept), not a second upload. 

Limits: 25 MB (HTML 5 MB); allowed types include pdf, office docs, csv/tsv, txt/md, json, html, zip, common audio/video, and images. svg/executables are rejected. URL expires in 10 minutes. Requires OAuth + edit access to the target.

HTML FILES (`text/html`): the body must start like an HTML document (`<!DOCTYPE`, `<html`, `<head` or `<body`). The file opens as a sandboxed artifact (scripts run, no network, no access to Fieldwerk) at the `viewer_url` this returns, `/f/<asset_id>` on the app. Who can open it is who can read where it's filed. To embed HTML inside a memo instead, use `get_memo_artifact_upload_url`.

content_type.description: MIME of the file you'll PUT, e.g. application/pdf.

filename.description: Original filename (used for the download name).

size.description: Byte size, if known (fail-fast quota check).

tools.name: add_link_asset
tools.title: Add link asset
tools.description: Add a LINK (a URL) to a memo (an attachment), or to a collection or notebook (it appears in the Files list). Exactly one target. Optionally set `title`/`description` yourself, and a free-text `summary` (a short write-up of what's at the link; this is the field your assistant is expected to author). No automatic fetching is done. Requires OAuth + edit access to the target.

url.description: http(s) URL to attach.

summary.description: Free-text summary of the destination (you, or the user, may write this).

tools.name: add_asset_from_url
tools.title: Add asset from URL
tools.description: Add a FILE to a memo (an attachment), or to a collection or notebook (a file in its Files list), by giving the server a URL to fetch. Exactly one target. Use this when you already have a hosted file URL (it sidesteps the MCP message-size cap and you don't need to PUT bytes yourself). The server fetches the URL with strict guardrails (https only, our own zones / private IPs denied, manual redirects, 25 MB cap (HTML 5 MB), 10-second timeout) and stores it. You MUST pass `content_type` (must be an allowed type: pdf, office docs, csv/tsv, txt/md, json, html, zip, audio/video, images). Returns the created asset. An HTML file (`text/html`) opens as a sandboxed artifact at the asset's `viewer_url` (`/f/<asset_id>` on the app). Requires OAuth + edit access to the target.

source_url.description: https URL of the file to fetch.

content_type.description: MIME of the file, e.g. application/pdf.

tools.name: backfill_link_asset
tools.title: Backfill link preview
tools.description: Fetch a LINK's URL (a link in a collection or notebook's Files, or a memo attachment) with a basic, NON-AI request and fill its empty title/description from the page's <title> / Open Graph / meta tags. Only fills fields you haven't already set; always records what was fetched. Requires edit access to the asset.

tools.name: list_assets
tools.title: List assets
tools.description: List the files and links on a collection or notebook (its Files), or the attachments on a memo. Exactly one target. Requires read access to it. WORDING: these tools say "asset" for any file or link. In the Fieldwerk UI, one added to a collection or notebook is a "file" (its list is headed Files), and one on a memo is an "attachment". Use those words with the user. FILES ARE ITEMS: in a collection or notebook each file can carry the collection's properties (status, assignee and so on, the same property definitions its memos use) and appears on boards and in list and table views. Each file in the response carries `fields` (its collection values, person values shown as names) and `file_type` ("PDF", "CSV", "PNG", "Link"...). A notebook file's values come from its collection. On a COLLECTION the default is its loose files only (in none of its notebooks); pass `include_notebook_files: true` for every file in the collection, each naming its `notebook` (null when loose). FILTER (collection or notebook only): `where` takes the same clause grammar as `list_collection_memos`, read against each file's collection values, plus the computed properties `computed:file_type` and `computed:item_kind` (always "File" here), as in a view's filters. `file_type` is a shortcut for one type ("pdf", "PDF" and "application/pdf" all work). Example, PDFs with status Draft: `file_type: "pdf", where: [{"field": "status", "equals": "Draft"}]`. To set a file's properties use `set_field` with `asset` and `collection`; to rename it, `update_asset`; to move it, `move_asset`. A memo's attachments carry no properties, so `where`, `file_type` and `include_notebook_files` are refused on a memo target.

where.description: Optional filter on a collection's or notebook's files: clauses that must ALL match, in the grammar `list_collection_memos` documents, read against each file's collection values. `computed:file_type` and `computed:item_kind` also work as fields. Person operands may be a name, an email or a user id.

scope.description: Optional. Which property the clause reads: "collection" for the collection's own value, "memo" for the memo's own front matter. Omitted, the clause reads front matter.

overlaps.description: For a date or Date range property: the value touches the window of days from `from` to `to` (YYYY-MM-DD, both inclusive, either left out for an open side). A single date counts as a one-day range. Example: everything in October 2026: `{"field": "dates", "overlaps": {"from": "2026-10-01", "to": "2026-10-31"}}`.

file_type.description: Optional: only files of this type, e.g. "pdf", "csv", "png", or "link" for links. Case-insensitive.

include_notebook_files.description: Collection target only. Default false (loose files only). True lists every file in the collection, including those in its notebooks, each with its `notebook`.

tools.name: get_asset
tools.title: Read asset
tools.description: Get one file's or link's metadata by its asset id (a collection or notebook file, or a memo attachment). For files the response includes a short-lived `download_url`; an HTML file also has `viewer_url`, where it opens as a sandboxed artifact. Readable if you can read any memo, collection or notebook it's on. A file's collection properties are not here: `list_assets` on its collection or notebook returns them.

tools.name: read_artifact
tools.title: Read an HTML artifact
tools.description:
Read an HTML artifact's source: an HTML file in a collection or notebook, or an artifact embedded in a memo. Pass ONE of: `asset` (its id), `url` (its `viewer_url` `/f/<id>`, or an older `artifact_url` `fieldwerkartifacts.com/a/<memo>/<id>`), or `memo` plus `artifact_id` (the `id=` in the memo's ```artifact block). Returns the HTML as text (large ones are truncated, `truncated: true`). Readable if you can see the file: an embedded artifact has its memo's access. Use it to check or revise an artifact before `replace_artifact`. 

VERSIONS: the response says which `version` you read and the `current_version`. If you can edit the artifact it also lists its `versions` (newest first: number, when, who, and `restored_from` for a restore); pass `version` to read an older one, e.g. to compare or to find the one to restore with `replace_artifact`'s `restore_version`. Every version counts toward workspace storage; `delete_asset` with `version` deletes an older one to free space.

url.description: Its viewer_url or an older artifact_url.

memo.description: Memo id or URL, with artifact_id.

artifact_id.description: The id= in the memo's artifact block.

version.description: Read this older version instead of the current one (edit access).

tools.name: replace_artifact
tools.title: Replace an HTML artifact
tools.description:
Replace an HTML artifact with a new version, keeping its link: an HTML file in a collection or notebook, or an artifact embedded in a memo. Everyone who opens its viewer_url, and the memo's embed, sees the new version; earlier versions are kept. Name it like `read_artifact` (`asset`, `url`, or `memo` + `artifact_id`) and pass ONE of:
  • `html`: the complete new document (self-contained, as for the upload tools; 1 MB for an embedded artifact, 5 MB for a file).
  • `restore_version`: an older version's number (from `read_artifact`'s `versions`) to bring back. It is copied in as a new version, so nothing is lost and it can be undone the same way.
Use this to revise an artifact instead of uploading a new one, so the memo doesn't gain a second block. Returns the new `version`. Requires OAuth and edit access to the file; a locked or archived memo's artifacts can't be changed.

url.description: Its viewer_url or an older artifact_url.

memo.description: Memo id or URL, with artifact_id.

artifact_id.description: The id= in the memo's artifact block.

restore_version.description: Instead of html: an older version number to make current again.

tools.name: update_asset
tools.title: Rename or describe a file
tools.description: Rename a file or link, or change its description or summary: a collection or notebook file, or a memo attachment. Pass only what you want to change; an empty string clears that one. `title` is the name the Files list, boards and views show (when it's empty they fall back to the original filename). `summary` is the free-text write-up of what's in the file or behind the link. This edits the file itself, everywhere it appears. A file's collection properties (status, assignee and so on) are separate: set those with `set_field` and `asset`. Requires OAuth and the right to manage the file: its owner, or edit access to a memo, collection or notebook it's on.

asset.description: Asset id of the file or link.

title.description: New name. Empty string clears it. Max 500 chars.

description.description: New description. Empty string clears it. Max 2000 chars.

summary.description: New free-text summary. Empty string clears it. Max 8000 chars.

tools.name: attach_asset
tools.title: Attach asset
tools.description: Add an EXISTING file or link to another memo (as an attachment), or to a collection or notebook (in its Files). Exactly one target. Gated by edit access to that target. This adds a place and leaves the file where it already is; to move a file from one collection or notebook to another, use `move_asset`.

tools.name: move_asset
tools.title: Move file
tools.description: Move a FILE between a collection and one of its notebooks, between two notebooks, or to another collection, in one step. Name where it is now with exactly one of `from_collection` / `from_notebook`, and where it goes with exactly one of `to_collection` / `to_notebook`. The file always ends up in exactly one place: if `from_collection` names a file that sits in one of that collection's notebooks, it moves out of that notebook; if it sits in several, the call is refused with their names and you pass `from_notebook` to pick one. The response's `from` says where it actually moved from. Within one collection the file keeps its collection properties, because a notebook file is still in its collection: moving it out of a notebook leaves it loose in the collection, and moving a loose file into a notebook keeps its values. Moving it to a DIFFERENT collection takes it out of the old one, and its values there go with that. Needs edit access to both ends, and OAuth. For a memo's attachments use `attach_asset` and `remove_asset` instead.

asset.description: Asset id of the file to move.

from_collection.description: Collection id the file is in now. If it sits in one of this collection's notebooks, the move is from that notebook.

from_notebook.description: Notebook id the file is in now.

to_collection.description: Collection id to move it to (loose, in none of its notebooks).

to_notebook.description: Notebook id to move it into.

tools.name: remove_asset
tools.title: Remove asset
tools.description: Remove a file or link from one memo (an attachment), collection or notebook (its Files). Exactly one target. The file itself is not deleted; use `delete_asset` for that. Gated by edit access to the target.

tools.name: delete_asset
tools.title: Delete asset
tools.description:
Permanently delete a file or link (a collection or notebook file, or a memo attachment). Only the file's owner can delete it. Removes it from every memo, collection and notebook it's on and frees its storage. Use `remove_asset` to only take it off one place. An HTML artifact embedded in a memo is part of that memo: deleting it also removes its block from the memo, and `remove_asset` refuses to take it off its memo.

Pass `version` to delete only that older version of an HTML artifact (numbers from `read_artifact`'s `versions`) and free its storage; the file and its link stay. The current version can't be deleted: restore another with `replace_artifact` first. Needs edit access, not ownership.

version.description: Delete only this older version, not the whole file.

tools.name: query_asset
tools.title: Query asset
tools.description: Query a CSV/TSV FILE by its asset id (a collection or notebook file, or a memo attachment): optional column projection, simple AND filters (eq / neq / contains), and a row limit. Returns matching rows as JSON plus `matched` (total before limit). Readable if you can read the file. Server-side parse, capped at 500 rows. For large datasets pull the columns/filters you need rather than the whole file.

tools.name: lock_memo
tools.title: Lock memo
tools.description: Lock a memo. While locked, no body, field, comment, or collection-membership writes succeed from any surface (REST, MCP, web). Reads continue to work normally and existing comments stay fully visible. Available to the owner or a member/collaborator with edit access, via Clerk OAuth. Idempotent: locking an already-locked memo returns the existing `locked_at`. To unlock, call `unlock_memo` and follow the returned URL — unlock cannot be done from MCP because the unlock action requires a human confirmation in the browser.

url.description: Memo URL. Either url or id is required.

tools.name: unlock_memo
tools.title: Unlock memo
tools.description:
Initiate unlocking a memo. Does NOT unlock from this tool — returns a one-shot URL the user must open in their browser, where the unlock confirmation dialog pops automatically and they have to click Unlock to confirm. This friction is deliberate: a locked memo is a protective intent the owner set, and an agent shouldn't be able to undo it for them.

Available to the owner or a member/collaborator with edit access, via Clerk OAuth. Use when the user asks you to unlock a memo. RELAY THE RETURNED `unlock_url` VERBATIM TO THE USER and tell them to open it; do not retry, do not call any write tool against this memo until they confirm they've unlocked it.

url.description: Memo URL. Either url or id is required.

tools.name: archive_memo
tools.title: Archive memo
tools.description: Archive a memo. The memo stays in place with access and memberships intact, but becomes read-only: no body, field, comment, or collection-membership writes succeed from any surface until it is unarchived. It is hidden from default lists and searches (pass `include_archived: true` to list tools to see it) and never appears in published collections. NOT the same as locking: archive is an organisational state, the lock is a protective one, and either freezes writes on its own. Available to the owner or a member/collaborator with edit access, via Clerk OAuth. Idempotent: archiving an already-archived memo returns the existing `archived_at`. Reversible with `unarchive_memo`.

url.description: Memo URL. Either url or id is required.

tools.name: unarchive_memo
tools.title: Unarchive memo
tools.description: Unarchive a memo: restore it to the normal editable state and back into default lists. The counterpart to `archive_memo`. Unlike `unlock_memo` this DOES perform the change: archive is an organisational state, not a protective one, so no browser confirmation is required. Available to the owner or a member/collaborator with edit access, via Clerk OAuth. Idempotent: unarchiving a memo that isn't archived is a no-op.

url.description: Memo URL. Either url or id is required.

tools.name: delete_memo
tools.title: Delete memo
tools.description: Delete a memo. CLAIMED memos go to the user's trash (recoverable from /trash) for a window that depends on the workspace's plan. Calling again on the same id while it's already in trash removes it from the user's trash view; the content is NOT destroyed early and is still permanently deleted on its existing schedule. UNCLAIMED memos are hard-deleted immediately. If the memo is unclaimed, edit access via its link is enough. If the memo is claimed, you must be signed in via OAuth as the owner. Edit access alone is not sufficient. LOCKED memos cannot be deleted (TRA-345): the lock contract holds for destructive ops, so the owner must `unlock_memo` first. Soft-delete (to trash) and the second-call removal from trash both apply this guard.

tools.name: claim_memo
tools.title: Claim memo
tools.description: Attach an orphan memo to your account. Requires OAuth. Pass the memo's edit URL (or id).

tools.name: transfer_memo_ownership
tools.title: Transfer memo ownership
tools.description: Transfer a memo to a new owner (CURRENT owner only). This changes only the owner, the memo stays in its current workspace. To MOVE a memo to a DIFFERENT workspace (optionally handing it to someone there at the same time), use `move_memo` instead. The new owner must be an existing Fieldwerk account (`new_owner_email`). You (the previous owner) are dropped to an Editor grant — you keep edit access but lose ownership and management. This is a deliberate, hard-to-undo action; confirm intent before calling. Requires OAuth.

tools.name: move_memo
tools.title: Move memo to workspace
tools.description: Move a memo to another workspace (CURRENT owner only). This is a MOVE, not a copy: the memo keeps its same id and its full edit history, versions, comments, reactions, images, and embedded artifacts all come with it. After the move the memo is removed from the source workspace entirely, and its link sharing and direct grants are reset to the destination's defaults. Identify the memo with `url` (or `id`). Pass `workspace` for the destination (a name, slug, or id from `list_workspaces`); it must differ from the memo's current workspace, and is required (a move places the memo into a specific workspace, never the one you last opened in the web app). When the user belongs to several workspaces, ask which destination they mean before calling, and remember that choice for the rest of the session. By default you become the new owner; pass `new_owner_email` to hand it to another member (they must be an active, non-guest member of the destination, as must you). Optionally file it into destination collections: `collection_ids` for existing ones, `new_collections` to create fresh ones (each a name, or { name, description? }), or `recreate_source_collections: true` to recreate the memo's current collections (name AND description) in the destination. New collections are owned by the new owner by default; pass `new_collection_owner_email` to assign them to another member (find people with `list_workspace_members`). Existing collections are left untouched. A workspace admin can turn moving content out of a workspace off (it is off by default): when it is, this tool changes nothing and answers `ok: false` with `error: "workspace_setting_disabled"`, which is a settled answer, not a transient failure. Do not retry it or reach for another tool to work around it; tell the person their workspace admin has to allow the move. This is a deliberate, hard-to-undo action; confirm intent before calling. Requires OAuth.
